newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares on Thursday extended Wednesday's gains in higher turnover and analysts expected more gains on Friday that could lead into next week.
"If there's no flood of supply on Friday then a light growth tendency should last into next week," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Analysts said the market could find resistance at about 14,000 points of the main index next week, still in its general month-long flat trend after having fallen slightly last week.
They said larger turnovers were still necessary to suggest large investors were buying enough to spur significant growth.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.3 percent to 13,691.2 points and turnover rose 20.1 percent to 96.5 million zlotys ($33.8 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 72 to five with six stocks stable.

Analysts said November's inflation figure due on Monday should not have a significant effect on the market as no interest-rate cut was seen forthcoming, though some analysts said any good news could have a greater effect next week.
Analysts said top gainers construction firm Remak and steel trader Stalexport, up 9.8 and 9.7 percent, saw speculative surges after recent falls and that no growth trend was in store for them.
They said the most active stock, trader Universal up 6.9 percent, could still be benefiting from its recent forecast of a 60-million-zloty ($21 million) group net in 1997.
Continuous trade turnover was at 5.8 million zlotys ($2 million) with three stocks falling, two rising and five flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 6.5 percent to 148 zlotys ($51.9) and fell 1.4 percent to 144.5 zlotys ($50.6) in 29.7-million-zloty ($10.4 million) live trade.
